## Inherited Must-Fix items (the planner MUST address ALL of these in v3)

### M1 — Per-cell `_wedged_run_inputs_on_hf` gate (Methodology, conclusion-changing)

The plan's auto-terminate is gated on `_wedged_run_inputs_on_hf` (§B.3 L445-450), which mirrors fix (a)'s `_cell_artifacts_on_hub` (§A.3 L105-114) "over the selected cells' raw-completion + store-tensor prefixes." But `_select_cells(args)` (issue664_dispatch.py L145-175) returns the **FULL static sweep set** (e.g. 32 cells), and the existing P3 helpers iterate over all of them. So a literal mirror requires ALL selected cells on HF — making the gate FAIL on a mid-sweep wedge (where only 10 of 32 are complete and 22 are not-yet-run), which is exactly the #664-class case the fix is designed for.

**Fix:** the planner must EITHER (a) define the gate per-cell with three states — COMPLETED cells require both raw+store prefixes on HF; PARTIAL cells (exactly one artifact-kind) BLOCK; NOT-YET-RUN selected cells are explicitly rerunnable-from-verified-inputs and DO NOT block — OR (b) downgrade the §0/§B.1 auto-migrate claim to "auto-terminate only after full-sweep upload" and drop the without-human-intervention mid-sweep promise. Pick one.

**Mechanizable verification:** `tests/test_runpod_wedge_detection.py` case with 32 selected cells, 10 having both prefixes on HF + 22 absent (not-yet-run), assert the gate ALLOWS terminate (per-cell policy) rather than blocking on the 22 missing.

### M2 — Fresh-listing Hub verify for `_upload_store_tensors` (Methodology, conclusion-changing)

The plan's §A.3 claim (L181-183) "The P3 fail-loud verify at the end stays — authoritative 'everything is on HF before teardown'" is **false for store tensors**: `_upload_store_tensors` (issue664_dispatch.py L1262-1285) only checks LOCAL `tp.exists()` and raises on a missing LOCAL file; it has NO fresh `list_repo_files` Hub-landing verify, unlike `_upload_raw_completions` L1236-1244 and `_upload_baseline_propensity` L1186-1195. Since fix (b)'s irreversible auto-terminate is gated on `_wedged_run_inputs_on_hf` checking store-tensor prefixes, a P3 that silently passes with store tensors uploaded-but-not-landed (429 throttle / transient `_upload` failure) lets an irreversible terminate proceed with the Phase-3/4 PRIMARY deliverable absent from HF (the #521 trap class the helper's own docstring at L1254-1259 explicitly warns against).

**Fix:** add a fresh-listing Hub verify to `_upload_store_tensors` and to the new per-cell store path; correct the §A.3 sentence to reflect that store tensors gain a NEW Hub-landing verify (not a "stays" claim).

**Mechanizable verification:** static/test check that `_upload_store_tensors` calls `list_repo_files` after the upload loop and raises when expected `C.HF_STORE_PREFIX/<cell>/...` entries are absent from a mocked fresh listing.

### S1 — Exact-file-set completeness (Statistics, conclusion-changing)

The plan's concrete skip sketch at §A.3 L194 is `if any(p.startswith(cell_prefix) for p in on_hub): continue` — pure prefix presence. The production terminal verify (issue664_dispatch.py L1188-1191 / L1237-1244) is also prefix-COUNT-based (`landed = [p ... if p.startswith(prefix)]; if len(landed) < n_expected`). Neither checks the exact expected file set including `tensors.pt`. A cell with one file under its prefix (interrupted mid-`upload_folder`, partial raw-completions write) would be SKIPPED as "present" and could pass the count-only verify. This completeness check propagates straight into `_wedged_run_inputs_on_hf` (the irreversible auto-terminate gate, §B.5 L503, headline safety claim §C.2 L559-568). Partial-read-as-complete → terminate → permanent data loss.

**Fix:** replace prefix-presence + count-only with EXACT expected-file-set completeness check (per cell: the cell's eval-JSON file set AND `tensors.pt` + its sibling store files) in BOTH `_cell_artifacts_on_hub` (the new skip guard) AND `_wedged_run_inputs_on_hf` (the auto-terminate gate). The exact expected file list per artifact-kind per cell must be enumerated in the plan.

**Mechanizable verification:** `tests/test_issue664_per_cell_upload.py` partial-on-Hub case (`list_repo_files` returns cell prefix but lacks an expected file like `tensors.pt`) → assert re-upload OR `RuntimeError`. Plus a `_wedged_run_inputs_on_hf` partial-cell case → returns False (no terminate).

### S2 — Malformed-clock fail-soft test (Statistics, conclusion-changing)

The plan asserts (§B.3 L369-371) the no-port clock helpers are "atomic tmp+rename, never raising ... same contract as the GCP clock." `_maybe_escalate_runpod_wedge` reads the clock at §B.3 L347. A malformed/non-numeric `runpod_noport_first_seen_ts` entry that makes the read raise crashes the poll tick — and a crashed tick on a RUNNING-but-no-port pod means no escalation, no terminate, billing leak persists silently (the exact #664 class). The §TDD list (L910-915) covers normal first/second tick, within-K, port-appears, status-leaves-RUNNING — but NOT a corrupt sidecar. The GCP analogue IS tested in `test_backend_poll.py`, so this is a one-case parity gap — but the gap matters because a regression (a read that DOES raise on garbage) would sail through the suite and silently re-introduce #664.

**Fix:** add `test_runpod_noport_clock_malformed_sidecar_never_raises` to `tests/test_runpod_wedge_detection.py` — write a malformed/non-numeric clock value into the `tmp_path` sidecar, stub live RunPod API as RUNNING + null ports, call `_maybe_escalate_runpod_wedge`, assert no exception is raised AND result is non-escalated/running (`status != "dead"`, no `terminate_pod` call). Mirror the GCP `_read_phase_clock` malformed-clock case already in `test_backend_poll.py`.

### A2 — HF-presence as P2/P3 resume key (Alternatives, conclusion-changing — DESIGN DECISION)

The plan claims HF is the durability surface that makes auto-terminate data-safe (§0 L33 "Prerequisite for fix (b)'s auto-terminate to be data-safe"; §A.1 L72 "loses at most one in-flight cell"). But P2's resume-skip predicate `_cell_extract_eval_done` (issue664_dispatch.py L1017-1028) keys on LOCAL paths only (`C.STORE_ROOT/.../tensors.pt` + `C.EVAL_ROOT/registry/<cell>`), and the P2 `WaveDispatcher` `is_done` lambda (L1431) calls it directly. After fix (b)'s auto-terminate + FRESH-pod re-provision (`_relaunch_fresh_runpod` provisions a NEW host), HF-complete cells are LOCALLY ABSENT on the fresh pod, so P2 re-runs every one of them (wasted compute), and P3 raw-completions upload can raise "NO raw completions" on the missing local files.
